rows.reasoning: Square both nonnegative sides: (x-7)^2≥9(x-2)^2, so (2x+1)(4x-13)≤0. Integer x are 0,1,2,3; their sum is 6.
The first quadratic has roots -2 and 3, hence a=1 and b=6. The second has discriminant 1-24<0 and positive leading coefficient, so it is never negative.
AB has slope -1/2, so its perpendicular bisector has slope 2. It passes through midpoint (1,3), giving y=2x+1.
For y=mx, distance from (1,3) is |m-3|/√(m²+1); setting it to 1 gives m=4/3, so ㄴ works. The line x=0 is also distance 1; y=0 and ㄱ do not work.
Completing squares gives (x+1)^2+(y-3)^2=10-k. This is a circle exactly when its radius squared is positive, so k<10.
A circle tangent to both axes and through (2,1) must have positive center (r,r); solving (2-r)^2+(1-r)^2=r^2 gives r=1 or 5. The centers are (1,1) and (5,5), whose distance is 4√2.
The difference is (k-1)x²-(k-1)x+4. For strict positivity for all real x, let t=k-1: t=0 works, while t>0 requires t²-16t<0, so 0≤t<16. Thus k=1,...,16, sixteen integers.
Using directed section formulas, ㄱ gives P=(2+c)/3=10-c, hence c=7 and is true. ㄴ fails for a=5,b=1,m=2,n=1; ㄷ is not an identity (the formulas give p=((3n-m)a+(m+n)b)/(2(m+n))).
With P=(t,2-t), equal squared distances to A and B give (t+2)^2+(1-t)^2=(t-3)^2+(-t-3)^2, hence t=13/2. Then a-b=13/2-(-9/2)=11.
Write P=A+t(B-A). The area ratio [OBP]/[OAP]=|1-t|/|t|=4. The extension point is t=-1/3 (the other solution lies inside AB). Then P=(-14/3,4/3), so b-a=6.
Equal areas with common altitude to BC mean D is the midpoint of BC, so D=(1,3). The line through A=(5,11) and D has slope 2 and equation y=2x+1.
AP has slope 1/2 and BP has slope 2/(4-n). Their product is -1, so 1/(4-n)=-1 and n=5. Since ∠APB=90°, the circumcenter is midpoint of AB, (5/2,2), and ab=5.
OA has length 5 and is parallel to 3x-4y=0. The line containing P is parallel and offset by 16, so its distance from OA is 16/5. Triangle area is (1/2)·5·(16/5)=8.
The radii to the tangent points make 60° at the center, so in the right triangle with hypotenuse OP and radius 3, OP=3/cos30°=2√3. The locus is a circle of circumference 2π·2√3=4√3π.
P,Q lie on the circle with diameter AB, whose center is (0,1) and radius squared is 15. Intersecting y=x-2 gives x²+(x-3)²=15, with root difference √21. The chord length squared is 2(√21)^2=42.
For midpoint M=(-1,3), AP²+BP²=2·PM²+AB²/2=2·PM²+10. The circle center is (3,0), radius 2, and its distance to M is 5, so PM ranges from 3 to 7. The minimum plus maximum is (18+10)+(98+10)=136.
The intersection roots have sum 2(a+2). The parabola vertex is C=(2,1). Thus m=(2a+6)/3, n=(2a²-2a+9)/3, and m-n=(-2a²+4a-3)/3, maximized at a=1 with k=-1/3. Hence |k+1|=2/3.
Reflect A across the x-axis to A'=(0,-15); then AP=PA'. The maximum of PA'-PB along the x-axis occurs at t=25/4, where PA'=65/4 and PB=13/4, so a=13 and P=(25/4,0). Therefore a+4b+16c=13+25=38.
The tangent at (4,3) to x²+y²=25 is 4x+3y=25. Its distance from the center (3,1) is |12+3-25|/5=2, so the tangent circle radius squared is k=4.

The first inequality restricts integer x to [-7,1]. For each q, count centers c=-p for which [c-q,c+q] overlaps this nine-integer interval in exactly seven integers. Counts by q=1,...,9 are 0,0,3,2,2,2,2,2,1, totaling 14.
The three intersections are (-1,-1), (6,6), and (2,-2). Using vectors (7,7) and (3,-1), the area is |7(-1)-7·3|/2=14.
